First, find the score of the second student:  
3 wrong out of 40 means 40 − 3 = 37 correct.  
Percentage = (37 / 40) × 100 = 92.5%.  

The first student scored 95%, which is higher than 92.5%.  
So the top score to beat is 95%.  

To get the highest score, Sierra must beat 95%.  
If the test has 40 questions, 95% of 40 = 0.95 × 40 = 38 questions correct.  
To have the highest score, she needs more than 38 correct, so 39 or 40.  

Since the problem asks "how many questions does she have to get right," the minimum is 39.

Final answer: Sierra
